To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy required to move a skid-steer robot on rigid terrains is mainly due to the dynamic friction between the tracks and the surface, and that the energy required by the motors is almost constant regardless of the track width.
the energy consumption of a skid-steer mobile robot is proportional to its weight and to the square of its velocity.

1) power consumption of skid-steer mobile robots is dominated by the power losses due friction and 2) power losses due to friction can be modeled from the point of view of both the rigid terrain and the motors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the power consumption of tracked vehicles on flat terrain and its implications on the navigation of outdoor mobile robots.
the modeling of the power consumption of skid-steer mobile robots on hard flat terrained.
the power consumption of skid-steer robots on rigid terrain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power consumption is mainly determined by the track width, which has a strong influence on the power losses.
the power losses due dynamic friction in skid-steered tracked vehicles on rigid terrain are negligible at walking speeds.
skid steering on flat hard terrain at walking speeds does not require much power, but that it does require a lot of torque.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in skid steering, the energy consumption is mainly due to the dynamic friction of the terrain.
the power losses due only to the frictional forces between the tracks and the terrain are negligible compared with the total power losses.
the power drawn by a rigid terrain is not a good measure for the energy consumed by the vehicle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the case of hard flat terrains, the energy consumption of skid steering is not as large as previously thought.
the power consumption of a skid-steer robot can be modeled with a good degree of accuracy, even for the dynamic friction losses.
skid steering is an energy-efficient way to move in hard flat surfaces, even at walking speeds.
